The present claim petition arises out of a road accident in which one Rahul @ Rahul Kumar, aged about 22 years, suffered fatal injury resulting in his death.

An application u/s 166(1) Motor Vehicle Act was accordingly filed by the claimants Smt. Asha Kumari (aged about 32 years) as dependent mother and Sh.Raghunandan (aged about 35 years) as dependent father of the deceased.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 06.01.2021 at about 11:00 p.m. victim along with one Vijay and Raj Bahadur was traveling in a car bearing no.HR-56B-2065 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) from Delhi to Noida.
The car being driven by Raj Bahadur at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner.

Vijay and victim Rahul asked driver Raj MACT No.238/2021 Asha Kumari & anr.
Vs. Raj Bahadur & ors.. Page no. 2 of 8 ss Bahadur to slow down and drive carefully but he did not pay any heed.
Due to the high speed, vehicle dashed into a tree and Rahul sustained grievous injuries.
He was removed to District Hospital, Noida where he was declared dead.
On 16.02.2021 matter was reported vide GD No.048, however no FIR was registered.
The present claim petition was then filed before this Tribunal.

3. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
4.
Respondent no.1 and 2 did not file any written statement despite opportunity.

Respondent no.3/insurance company has refuted its liability on the ground that no FIR has been lodged in the present case and even the GD entry has been made only on 16.02.2021 i.e. after more than one month whereas the alleged accident occurred on 06.01.2021.
It is further pleaded that as per GD entry, the alleged accident was 'ittefaqia' i.e. due to chance, meaning thereby that there was neither rashness nor negligence of the alleged offending vehicle.

It is further pleaded that the particulars of the offending vehicle have been planted in the case/ It is further pleaded that the deceased was travelling as a gratuitous passenger and thus insurance company is not liable to compensate.

5. Vide order dated 13.07.2023 following issues were framed:
1) Whether the deceased suffered fatal injuries in a road traffic accident on 06.01.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-56B-2065 MACT

proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.

Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and MACT No.238/2021 Asha Kumari & anr. Vs. Raj Bahadur &

sentences.text: In the present case, petitioners have examined Sh. Vijay/PW1 as an eye witness.
PW-1 has deposed that he was travelling in the offending vehicle with the victim.
He was deposed the factum and manner of accident by claiming that the vehicle was being driven rashly at a very high speed due towhich its driver lost control and hit against a tree.
During cross examination PW-2 admitted that he was known to the victim as well as the driver prior to the accident as they all were from the same village.
He further conceded that while victim sustained fatal injuries, no MLC of PW-2 was prepared despite claiming to have sustained internal injuries.

There is also no material to show that while the accident caused such grave injuries to victim who was sitting on the seat next to the driver,
such driver of the offending vehicle did not even suffer a scratch or injury for which he would have had to obtain treatment/first aid.
There is no medical record that the doctor treating the victim was informed about any Road Traffic accident.

Apart from a complainant filed by the father of victim, 36 days after the accident, there is no contemporary document to prove that the death of the victim was due to an accident involving the offending vehicle.

It is particularly doubtful that despite alleging no serious injuries, PW-2 Vijay did not inform the police or even any of the family members of the deceased nor any of the family members of the deceased nor did he accompany the victim to the MACT No.238/2021 Asha Kumari & anr. Vs. Raj Bahadur & ors..

. It is perhaps therefore that no efforts for even registration of FIR were made by the complainant.
There is thus, no material or evidence to show that the driver of of the offending vehicle was driving at a high speed or in a rash or negligent manner.
There is no evidence that the offending car dashed into any three.
There is no mechanical inspection report of the vehicle.
PW2 has further contradicted his own version by stating in his cross examination that the accident may have occurred due to sudden appearance of a cow or due to jumping on the speed braker.
His version further contrary to the version of father of the victim as per whome the accident occurred due to fog and crashing into a tree.
The entire story of the petitioners, thus, seems to have been concocted, which therefore resulted in a delay in reporting and was therefore never be registered into an FIR.
The untimely death of the victim is certainly unfortunate however there is lack of evidence to prove of such death was even due to a road accident.
The delay in filing a complaint, contradictions in the manner of accident and reasons discussed above fail to inspire any truth therein.
As such, issue no. is decided against the petitioners.
